corrections.claim: 3.6, 'Why it is needed in addition to G3': "G3 compares printed text, and only the user's own declarations. G4 compares terms against the freeze, so it also covers statements that Claude formalised in this run."
corrections.problem: Wrong. G3's statement-changed rule compares every frozen non-theorem declaration of the subject. That includes the statements, `.holds` axioms and vocabulary Claude wrote before the freeze, not only the user's declarations. The real difference between G3 and G4 is printed text versus terms, plus G4's kernel replay.
corrections.correct_statement: G3 compares printed text (default pp, implicit and instance arguments hidden) in two ways. existing-changed compares against B, i.e. the user's declarations. statement-changed compares against F, i.e. every non-theorem declaration of the subject at the freeze, Claude's formalisations included. G4 compares terms: T.holds's type, its closure and the permitted axioms' types against the frozen export. It also replays the export in the kernel. That is why G4 is authoritative.
corrections.evidence: packages/core/src/gate/permitted.ts snapshotOf keeps every declFacts entry of the subject's files whose kind is not theorem. rules.ts:437 loops over freeze.declarations. packages/core/test/gate/rules.test.ts:288 is titled 'statement-changed: a frozen statement new in the run changes after the freeze'.

corrections.claim: 3.6 existing-changed 'Blocks: … an `open … in`, a section `variable` or a new instance that changes what unchanged text elaborates to'. Also 3.7 item 1 safeguard: 'statements that the user formalised before the run cannot be changed by the run (`existing-changed`, `markup`, G4)'.
corrections.problem: Overstated, and it contradicts the draft's own 3.7 item 7. The meaning check compares default `#check`/`#print` output (only pp.fullNames and pp.proofs false are set), and that output hides instance arguments. Suppose Claude adds an instance before the freeze that changes how the user's unchanged text elaborates. The printed text stays the same. A TC-resolved instance is not an .ilean reference, so it is never flagged as a definition. G4 compares against a freeze that already contains the change. G4 protects only against changes made after the freeze.
corrections.correct_statement: existing-changed catches changes to the text and to the printed type or value. That covers most `open … in` and `variable` effects. It misses an elaboration change that prints the same, typically a new instance added before the freeze. In that case the meaning of a statement the user formalised before the run can change unnoticed. G4 only covers changes made after the freeze.
corrections.evidence: Lean 4.35 scratch file. `abbrev A.s : Prop := (1 : Nat) + 1 = 2`, then `instance (priority := high) myAdd : Add Nat := ⟨fun _ _ => 0⟩`, then `abbrev B.s` with the identical text. `#print` gives `@[reducible] def A.s : Prop := 1 + 1 = 2`, and B.s prints the same. `#check` gives `Prop` for both. Yet `example : A.s := rfl` and `example : ¬ B.s := by decide` both compile. Code: runner/src/semantic/checkFile.ts sets only those two options. rules.ts existing-changed compares norm(type)/norm(value). flagged() follows only facts refs.

corrections.claim: 3.4: "proved(v) ⟺ (1) Lean has facts for H_v (fresh, or kept from a stale file); (2) H_v is not an axiom; (3) ⌜type(H_v)⌝ = ⌜n⌝; (4) sorryAx ∉ Ax(H_v)."
corrections.problem: The ⟺ omits a precondition. The card must be bound to a statement that exists and is a Prop abbrev/def, with no TL101 or TL113. Otherwise build.ts never computes a proof status, which stays `none`, even when n.holds is a sorry-free theorem whose printed type is n. Condition (1) also needs facts that carry both a type and an axiom list.
corrections.correct_statement: proved(v) ⟺ (0) v is bound (pinned or adjacent) to a statement n that is found and is a Prop abbrev/def; (1) usable facts for H_v with a type and an axiom list; (2)–(4) as stated.
corrections.evidence: packages/core/src/project/build.ts:546 `if (!draft.statementFound || draft.notProp || !statement) continue;` comes before the proof table. `hk = draft.statementFound && !draft.notProp ? holdsKind(draft) : undefined`. Without hk, permitted.ts contribution() treats such a premise as unusable.

corrections.claim: 3.7 item 7 and the gap claim: 'In a round that finishes with any status other than proved, Claude can delete the user's existing proof of T, or turn it into `axiom T.holds : T`, without any finding.'
corrections.problem: True for deletion at any time. For conversion it holds only before freeze_statements, or in a round that never freezes. A conversion after the round's freeze is caught: T.holds was a theorem in the frozen model, so it is not in F's axiom list, and new-axiom fires (token `belief`). The after-freeze check runs before the inBase skip.
corrections.correct_statement: Claude can delete the user's proof of T at any point. It can turn the proof into `axiom T.holds : T` before freezing, or in a round without a freeze, in either case with no finding. The same conversion after the freeze is refused by new-axiom.
corrections.evidence: rules.ts:279 `if (frozenAxioms) { if (frozenAxioms.has(name)) continue; push(...) }` comes before rules.ts:291 `if (inBase(name) …) continue`. I reproduced this with a scratch probe that bundles the real core rules with test/gate/helpers/spyroRun.ts, using B = the honest proof. Results: delete, gate-other → []. To axiom without a freeze → []. To axiom after a freeze taken while it was a theorem → ["new-axiom:belief"]. Freeze rules on the converted state → []. gate-other after freezing that state → [].

corrections.claim: Central claim: '…and the proof is checked against statements frozen before any proof existed.' 3.6 proof-before-freeze: 'Blocks: choosing the statements to fit a proof that has already been found'.
corrections.problem: Overstated. proof-before-freeze refuses only proofs added or changed since the round start R. Proofs in B can exist before the freeze. So can proofs Claude wrote in earlier rounds of the same run, because Feedback keeps the working copy and sets R to the current head. From round 2 on, Claude may revise its own round-1 formalisations, which are not in B and therefore not protected by existing-changed, while knowing its round-1 proofs.
corrections.correct_statement: The proof is checked against statements frozen before any proof was written or changed in the current round. D-19's separation holds within a round. It does not hold across Feedback rounds.
corrections.evidence: rules.ts:683 compares S with `R = declTables(roundStart ?? base)`. manager.ts:1499 feedbackNow sets `run.p.roundStartCommit = head.id` with no revert. existing-changed iterates B.byName only.

corrections.claim: 3.3: '**A new axiom whose type is a proposition**, other than the `.holds` of a selected assumption (rule `new-axiom`).'
corrections.problem: Inaccurate. The rule is defined by 'not vocabulary', not by Prop-ness. Before the freeze it also allows two Prop-typed axioms: adopted ghosts' `.holds`, and new presupposition axioms `axiom T.exists : Nonempty T` for a project sort. A presupposition counts as vocabulary of kind presupposition and becomes a definition question. Conversely, non-Prop axioms that are bound to a card, or that cannot be classified, are refused.
corrections.correct_statement: Before the freeze, every new axiom must be one of: the `.holds` of a selected ASSUMPTION or adopted ghost, or a vocabulary item of its own (bound to no card, not unmarked-axiom). Presuppositions are allowed and flagged. After the freeze, no new axiom is allowed.
corrections.evidence: rules.ts notVocabulary() returns undefined for every vocabulary kind except unmarked-axiom. Probe: a new `axiom Toy : Type`, `axiom Toy.exists : Nonempty Toy` and its instance gives check/formalise findings [] and flaggedDefinitions ["Spyro.Toy.exists"].

corrections.claim: 3.6 missing-holds invariant: 'every formalised selected ASSUMPTION and every ghost has a `.holds` axiom stating exactly it.'
corrections.problem: The code does not require an axiom. It requires only that a `.holds` exists without holds-mismatch. A theorem `.holds`, i.e. the user's own provable assumption, passes. Such a premise then contributes its proof's footprint through DF, not through Sel.
corrections.correct_statement: …has a `.holds` whose printed type is exactly its statement. The `axiom n.holds : n` form is what the message asks for, but it is not checked.
corrections.evidence: rules.ts:614 and rules.ts:625 test only `justification === undefined` and the `holds-mismatch` flag. Probe: in B, cynder_dark_past.holds is `theorem … := dark_src`. The freeze rules on the normative state give [].

corrections.claim: 3.6 ghost single-term rule keyword list (axiom, theorem, …, open, export, omit, include, @[).
corrections.problem: Incomplete. The list omits `coinductive`, which GHOST_COMMAND_WORDS contains.
corrections.correct_statement: The list includes `coinductive`.
corrections.evidence: packages/core/src/gate/g0.ts:245 `'coinductive'`. docs/decisions-log.md §18 also lists `coinductive`.

corrections.claim: 3.9 table: 'Accept: … `runner/src/proposal/service.ts` `planAccept`, `MERGE_CONTEXT_LINES` (3)'. The claims list makes the same attribution.
corrections.problem: Wrong location. MERGE_CONTEXT_LINES and the no-fuzz merge (mergeFile) are in files.ts, not service.ts.
corrections.correct_statement: `runner/src/proposal/files.ts` `MERGE_CONTEXT_LINES`, `mergeFile` (planAccept in service.ts calls them).
corrections.evidence: packages/runner/src/proposal/files.ts:18 `export const MERGE_CONTEXT_LINES = 3;`. files.ts:70–71 call structuredPatch with context 3 and applyPatch with fuzzFactor 0.

corrections.claim: 3.6 new-axiom 'Blocks: … new vocabulary after the freeze'.
corrections.problem: Only vocabulary declared as an axiom (sorts, predicates, presuppositions) is blocked after the freeze. A new `noncomputable opaque` constant or function, or a definition, can still be added after the freeze. These are not axioms, statement-changed covers only frozen declarations, and only footprint judges them.
corrections.correct_statement: After the freeze, no new axiom may be added, so no new sorts, predicates or presuppositions. New opaque constants, functions and definitions are still possible and are held only to the footprint rule.
corrections.evidence: Probe with a freeze taken on the normative state. Adding `noncomputable opaque spyro : Character` plus the honest proof gives gate-proved []. Adding `axiom Hmm : Character → Prop` gives ["new-axiom:after-freeze"].

corrections.claim: 3.2: 'Presuppositions are the only existence assumptions a proof may use without the user selecting a card for them. Even then, only the sorts mentioned by the target's statement or a selected premise's statement count.' 3.6 also says 'For P = ∅ … given the existence of the sorts it mentions'.
corrections.problem: Imprecise on three counts. First, Pre is the set of presupposition axioms in the statements' `#print axioms`, i.e. the sorts of the named opaque constants a statement uses, not every sort it mentions. The draft's own 3.2 notes that `∀ g c, …` presupposes nothing. Second, DF can add further presuppositions from a selected user-proved derivation's footprint, for example a TL108 existence commitment. Third, Sig admits the user's axiom-declared constants, which are existence claims.
corrections.correct_statement: A proof may use presup(T) ∪ presup(selected), the presuppositions inside DF, and any existence claims in the user-trusted signature. Non-proof declarations may use any presupposition.
corrections.evidence: build.ts sets `lean.presupposes` from statementFacts.axioms filtered by isPresupposition. permitted.ts adds DF footprints unfiltered. signatureAxioms() includes kind constant/function even when declared with axiom. rules.ts allowedForOthers adds all presuppositions.

corrections.claim: 3.1: 'Stance and rationale have no logical effect. Lean, the statuses and the gate never read them.'
corrections.problem: 'No logical effect' is right, but the second sentence is not. The status flag `no-rationale` (TL011) comes from a missing rationale, and its message depends on stance. The gate's G5 reads both fields to require them byte-identical.
corrections.correct_statement: They have no logical effect. They feed only the `no-rationale` chip/flag (TL011, worded by stance), the G5 'unchanged' comparison, and the context sent to Claude.
corrections.evidence: build.ts `if (draft.type === 'ASSUMPTION' && block.fields.rationale === undefined) draft.flags.add('no-rationale')`. markup/values.ts noRationaleMessage(stance). rules.ts COMPARED_FIELDS includes rationale and stance.

corrections.claim: 3.2 project defaults: 'autoImplicit = false and relaxedAutoImplicit = false. Otherwise a typo such as `HasDarkPast cyndr` silently becomes a universally bound variable. TL110 warns when they are on.'
corrections.problem: TL110 inspects only `autoImplicit`: it is on when any `true` is present or no `false` is set. relaxedAutoImplicit is not read. Also, in the card statement form `abbrev n : Prop := HasDarkPast cyndr` the proposition is in the value, where auto-bound implicits do not apply, so the typo is an error. Silent binding happens only in declaration headers, such as theorem or axiom types and binders.
corrections.correct_statement: TL110 warns when autoImplicit is on or not switched off. A typo becomes an auto-bound variable only in header positions. In the statement abbrev's value it is an 'Unknown identifier' error.
corrections.evidence: packages/core/src/project/lakefile.ts matches only /\bautoImplicit\s*=…/. Lean 4.35 scratch with autoImplicit and relaxedAutoImplicit both true: `abbrev s1 : Prop := HasDarkPast cyndr` gives 'Unknown identifier `cyndr`', while `theorem s2 : HasDarkPast cyndr` elaborates to `∀ {cyndr : Character}, HasDarkPast cyndr`.

corrections.claim: 3.4 footprint mapping: 'a sort, a predicate, or a constant or function declared `opaque`: dropped (these are symbols, not beliefs)'.
corrections.problem: The opaque case can never occur. `#print axioms` lists only axioms, so opaque-declared constants and functions never appear in Ax. In practice sorts and predicates are dropped, and a constant or function declared with `axiom` becomes `axiom:<name>` with TL103.
corrections.correct_statement: Axiom-declared sorts and predicates are dropped. Opaque constants never appear. A constant or function declared with `axiom` is shown as `axiom:` with TL103.
corrections.evidence: build.ts:627 `harmless` tests declaredWithAxiom. The Lean output for cynder_dark_past lists no `Spyro.cynder`.

corrections.claim: 3.4: 'existence-commitment (TL108): the footprint contains a presupposition that neither the card's own statement nor the statement of any footprint card presupposes.'
corrections.problem: Incomplete. For a conditional proof, the presuppositions of the hypothesis cards (`on`) also count as covered.
corrections.correct_statement: …neither the card's statement, nor any footprint card's statement, nor (for a conditional proof) any hypothesis card's statement presupposes.
corrections.evidence: build.ts:660 `covered = … [...footprintNodes, ...onNodes]…`.

corrections.claim: 3.6 'What does gate Accept': the definition questions, the review (which shows statements before the proof result), the lifecycle ticks, and new vocabulary.
corrections.problem: Only the definition approvals are enforced. The host refuses Accept without them and the button is disabled. The review hides the result until the statements are gone through, but it has a 'Show the proof result now' button, and Accept is 'always at hand'. Lifecycle items are optional. Vocabulary is auto-approved.
corrections.correct_statement: Accept requires a 'yes' to every definition question. The review's meaning-before-result order is a UI default, not a precondition of Accept.
corrections.evidence: manager.ts acceptNow checks only missingDefinitions. webview/src/run/Review.tsx: Accept is `disabled={!approved || busy !== null}`, and the header comment says 'Accept / Feedback / Discard / Raw Lean diff always at hand'. The revealResult button is at Review.tsx:177 and :330.

corrections.claim: 3.8 Reading A step 7: 'Accept writes the formalisation, the proof and `type: DERIVATION`.'
corrections.problem: The type change happens only if the user ticks the optional, recommended lifecycle item l1.
corrections.correct_statement: Accept writes the formalisation and the proof, and `type: DERIVATION` when 'Make it a Derivation' is ticked (the e2e test ticks it).
corrections.evidence: service.ts planAccept applies only `ticked` lifecycle items. normalise.ts lifecycle().

corrections.claim: Claims list: "The status flags 'broken', 'depends-on-removed', 'unselected-used' and 'signoff-stale' are defined and displayed but never set by core."
corrections.problem: Only broken and depends-on-removed have a chip. unselected-used and signoff-stale are not displayed anywhere. 'Never set' is correct for all four.
corrections.correct_statement: All four are defined in StatusFlag/FLAG_ORDER and never set. Only 'broken' (also used for depends-on-removed) has a webview chip, which the user guide §7 lists.
corrections.evidence: grep finds them only in model.ts:137-143, build.ts FLAG_ORDER and webview/src/model/cardData.ts:169.

corrections.claim: 3.6 sorry-axiom invariant: '…except the user's own unchanged declaration that already used sorry in B.'
corrections.problem: Incomplete. When B has no facts (Accept's re-check after drift), every declaration whose text is unchanged is exempt, whether or not it used sorry in B.
corrections.correct_statement: …except an unchanged-text declaration that used sorry in B, or any unchanged-text declaration when B has no facts.
corrections.evidence: rules.ts:565 `if (base.facts === undefined || bf?.usesSorry === true || …) continue;`.

corrections.claim: 3.6 retry loop 'Invariant: what the proposal shows is always a judged state', after a revert ('normalises that state, re-checks it (not counted), and builds the proposal from it').
corrections.problem: Needs a nuance. The post-revert re-check uses purpose `check`, and the proposal is built whatever that check reports. The reverted commit itself passed a gate or the freeze rules, or is B. The shown state is that commit plus telelean's normalisation, not a state judged by the gate.
corrections.correct_statement: The proposal shows the newest commit that passed a gate (gate-pass) or the freeze rules (freeze), or B, plus telelean's pins and docstrings. The re-check only supplies facts and is not blocking.
corrections.evidence: manager.ts settleReverted: `check = await this.o.services.engine.check(ctx)` (manager.ts:1123), then buildProposal(...) unconditionally.

corrections.claim: Claims list: 'G0 … using the Lean lexer so comments, strings and blocks never count.'
corrections.problem: Misleading wording. G0 uses telelean's own TypeScript lexer (`lexLean`), not Lean's lexer or parser. The draft's 3.7 itself says a Lean-parser-checked G0 is deferred to H.
corrections.correct_statement: G0 uses telelean's TypeScript Lean lexer (core markup/lexer.ts lexLean). Only its tokens count.
corrections.evidence: packages/core/src/gate/g0.ts imports lexLean from '../markup/lexer.js'.

missing: freeze_statements may succeed only once per round. After it, the stage is 'prove' and toolFreeze refuses ('already frozen in this round; statements change only after the person's feedback'). Statements can be re-frozen only through Feedback (a new formalise round) or ghost adoption. Source: manager.ts:1983.

The check budget telelean.run.maxChecks (default 25 per round) is enforced. check_lean, freeze_statements and each propose_assumption count one. Once the budget is used up, these tools throw 'check budget used up … call finish'. This does not end the round. Source: manager.ts assertCheckBudget.

existing-changed has a second clause the draft does not mention. An adopted ghost's statement abbrev and its `.holds` axiom are held to their text at A, the newest adopt commit (token `ghost`). G5 separately holds the ghost's block to A.

Proofs from earlier rounds survive Feedback, since the working copy is not reverted and R becomes the head. The 'formalise, freeze, prove' separation therefore holds per round, and Claude's own earlier formalisations are protected by nothing in the next round.

The pre-freeze instance blind spot (an elaboration change that prints identically) affects statements the user formalised before the run, not only Claude's. It is a gap in the faithfulness safeguards of 3.7 item 1. Verified with Lean 4.35: identical #print and #check output, opposite truth values.

The signature also admits the user's own shape-violating predicates and constants. signatureAxioms tests only that the kind is in SIGNATURE_KINDS and ignores the `shape-violation` flag. Its non-vocabulary branch covers any non-Prop axiom outside the subjects' files (not only Model.lean) and requires Lean to have typed it (typeSort known).

Vocabulary is computed only for declarations in subject modules. A library-root declaration is never a vocabulary item. That is why a library-root non-Prop axiom shows as `axiom:` with TL103 on the board while the gate admits it.

Accept without drift runs no check at all. It applies the judged state as one history entry, with one undo step only if a file changes. An Accept that changes no file records the outcome only, with no history entry and no undo step (decisions-log §27).

Stale facts are kept by name while the declaration's current keyword agrees with the old facts' kind (kindsAgree), not literally while the keyword is unchanged. For example, abbrev to def keeps the facts.

walkthrough.e2e.test.ts checks each cheat's first failure by category (gateCheckOf, e.g. `- statement_unchanged:`), not by exact finding code. The exact codes in 3.8's table come from the fixtures' `expect` fields and are pinned in core tests (rules.test.ts, premiseCheats.test.ts, carriers.test.ts).

The normative proof has the stated 11 axioms. The literal ghost check has 12 (+Spyro.InGame). The adopted round-2 proof has 13 (+Spyro.not_in_game_not_good.holds). pg_no_dark_past presupposes nothing. The countermodel example compiles. `theorem … : ¬ GoodAddition cynder newSpyro` prints its unfolded type, so it would get TL114.
